articles.title: Brazil’s President Lula Accuses Meta of Helping His Right-Wing Opponent
articles.description: With a narrow presidential election looming, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and his allies claim Meta is trying to give his right-wing rival an advantage.

articles.title: Why Trump Made a Diesel Deal With Putin
articles.description: Our national security and White House correspondent David E. Sanger breaks down why President Donald Trump struck a deal with President Vladimir V. Putin to import Russian diesel fuel in the coming months, despite having signed recent congressional legislation tightening energy sanctions on Russia.

articles.title: Burnham Pledges to Back Zelensky as Trump’s Ukraine Support Wavers
articles.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky, who met with Britain’s prime minister, has said Ukraine received no warning of Russian attacks, but President Trump has said Washington is still “sharing intel.”

articles.title: Turkey Raids Pro-Opposition TV Station
articles.description: The government appointed an overseer to the last big news channel critical of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. The authorities have now replaced the leadership at five major news outlets.

articles.title: As Pope Leo Recovers From Surgery, Messages of Support Abound at Rome Hospital
articles.description: The pontiff, 71, is expected to spend about a week in the hospital recovering from surgery that found lung cancer. Messages of support have flooded in from far and wide.

articles.title: China’s Exports Soar, Putting Its Trade Surplus on Track for a Record
articles.description: China’s exports grew last month at the fastest pace in almost any month since the end of the global financial crisis.

articles.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle’s Rise and Fall as Trump’s Ambassador to Greece
articles.description: President Trump cut her loose after damaging news reports about her tenure as ambassador to Greece. Once a prominent Trump insider, she suggested she will now fight to defend her reputation.

articles.title: Dalí Book Cover Stolen in France
articles.description: Three thieves broke into a private museum in central France and took off with a 330-pound book cover created by the surrealist master Salvador Dalí.

articles.title: ‘Why Did They Kill Him?’ Mourning Victims of Houthi Attack on a Saudi Airport
articles.description: The strike was the Iran-backed militia’s most lethal against Saudi Arabia, by far, during their long conflict.

articles.title: From Allies to Enemies: Ethiopia and Eritrea Edge Toward War
articles.description: The two nations fought alongside each other during a brutal conflict in Tigray that left hundreds of thousands of people dead just a few years ago. Now they are on the brink of fighting each other.

articles.title: Ukraine Says It Received No Intelligence About Strikes 2 Nights in a Row
articles.description: Asked about apparent U.S. threats to cut off intelligence sharing with Kyiv, which can warn of Russian aerial attacks, President Trump said information continued to flow.

articles.title: Leo XIV’s Lung Cancer Diagnosis Tests a Papacy Still Taking Shape

articles.title: Indian Protesters Describe Rough Treatment by the Police
articles.description: Some of those detained accused security forces of beating them during an intense crackdown on demonstrations in India’s capital over the weekend. Police have said they followed the law.

articles.title: The Taliban Suspend BBC Broadcasts Across Afghanistan
articles.description: The Taliban government has intensified its crackdown on the press in recent months but had so far targeted Afghan news outlets.

articles.title: Argentina’s President Has a Dog Psychic. Meet Celia Melamed.

articles.title: Pope Leo’s Cancer Surgery Draws Outpouring From World Leaders
articles.description: The pontiff’s illness also prompted calls for people to seek medical treatment and early cancer screenings.

articles.title: Pope Leo Has Lung Cancer, Vatican Says

articles.title: ‘The Assassin(s)’ Movie Fuels South Korea’s Culture Wars
articles.description: The film, “The Assassin(s),” revisits a 1974 shooting that has spawned J.F.K.-style conspiracy theories, exposing divides over the country’s history.

articles.title: Trump Hands Victories to Putin, Who Offers More War in Return
articles.description: Russia has reaped a diesel deal and an increase in U.S. pressure on Ukraine as President Trump’s political needs align with his longstanding inclinations toward Russia.

articles.title: Trump Squeezes Ukraine, Again

articles.title: Saudi Energy Giant Struck as War Spikes Between Houthis and Saudi Arabia
articles.description: The attack came after the Yemeni militia warned it would attack the headquarters of Aramco. The Saudi-led coalition said it was targeting Houthi capabilities.

articles.title: Senators Urge Trump to Reverse Diesel Deal With Putin
articles.description: A bipartisan group of 12 senators called on the president to drop his decision to ease sanctions on Russia’s exports of diesel fuel, saying the deal would help Moscow continue the war in Ukraine.

articles.title: A Father’s Mission Is to Show the World ‘What Russia Did to My Family’

articles.title: Russia Detains Japanese Journalist for Alleged Espionage

articles.title: Acclaimed Author Denies Using A.I. but Admits Plagiarism
articles.description: Breaking a weekslong silence, Thélyson Orélien, a Haitian-Canadian writer, still rejected accusations about his new novel, ‘It Was Either That or Die.’

articles.title: Bulgaria Summons Russian Ambassador After More Black Sea Drone Strikes

articles.title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

articles.title: Mother of Henry Nowak killer could be deported
articles.description: Kiran Kaur was found guilty of assisting an offender and was jailed for three years in July.

articles.title: 6 Members of South Africa’s Biggest Party Are Killed in Shootings
articles.description: The two shootings took place only a few weeks before pivotal, nationwide local elections, and as the party, the A.N.C., is embroiled in a dispute over the eligibility of more than 100 candidates.

articles.title: Severe drought declared in parts of southern England

articles.title: 20 Hours After Falling Overboard, Cruise Passenger Is Rescued Near Greece
articles.description: According to Greek officials, the woman told her rescuers she had jumped off the ship because she “wanted to disembark.”

articles.title: Dublin Hotel Accused of Revoking Bookings for an Event to Combat Antisemitism
